name: Burraco Italian
description: Burraco is an immensely popular Italian Rummy game related to Canasta. Four players in partnerships meld sets and sequences to create burracos (7+ card melds). The game features pozzetti (extra hands) and has been standardized by the Federazione Italiano Burraco since the 1990s.
players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (standard); 2-5 player individual variants exist

overview.description: Burraco is an immensely popular Italian Rummy game related to Canasta. Four players in partnerships meld sets and sequences to create burracos (7+ card melds). The game features pozzetti (extra hands) and has been standardized by the Federazione Italiano Burraco since the 1990s.

history.origins: Burraco originated in South America (probably 1940s) and was adapted in Italy. Since the 1990s it has become extremely popular in Italy with an active tournament scene and the establishment of the Federazione Italiano Burraco which standardized the rules.
timeline: 1990s-present: Federazione Italiano Burraco established; rules standardized
2000s-present: Active tournament scene and competitive leagues
history.cultural: Burraco is one of the most popular card games in Italy, played in homes, clubs, and competitive tournaments. The Federazione Italiano Burraco organizes national championships and maintains official rules.
history.evolution: The Italian version standardized rules that were more variable in South American versions. Key differences from Brazilian Buraco include the dealing method (cutting and forming pozzetti differently) and specific card values.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships; 2-5 player variants exist
setup.deck: 108 cards: two standard 52-card packs with 4 jokers (jolly). Twos (pinelle) can be wild or natural.
setup.dealing: Dealer chosen by drawing cards (lowest deals). Dealer deals 11 cards each from bottom portion. Cutter takes top third (~22+ cards), deals two 11-card pozzetti from bottom alternately, stacks them crosswise. Remaining cards form draw pile (41 cards) with one face-up card.
setup.equipment: Double deck with jokers, score sheet, table space

rules.objective: Form melds (sets or sequences) and create burracos (7+ card melds). Be first team to go out after taking pozzetto and having at least one burraco. Score points from melded cards plus bonuses.
rules.gameplay: Turn: draw from stock or take entire discard pile; optionally meld sets (3+ same rank) or sequences (3+ consecutive same suit) or add to team melds; discard one card. First player to empty hand takes a pozzetto (11-card extra hand). Direct pozzetto: meld all cards, take pozzetto, continue. Indirect: meld all but one, discard, take pozzetto face down, use next turn.
keyRules: 108 cards: 2 decks + 4 jokers; twos are wild (pinelle)
Two 11-card pozzetti set aside for first players out
Sets: 3+ cards same rank, max 1 wild, max 9 cards
Sequences: 3+ consecutive same suit, max 1 wild
Ace can be high or low but not both in same sequence
Need burraco and taken pozzetto to go out

strategy.basic: Focus on creating your first burraco quickly. Use jokers and twos wisely to complete difficult melds. Take pozzetto when you have a strong position. Watch partner's melds to coordinate.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played and discarded. Time your pozzetto take carefully - direct take lets you use cards immediately; indirect hides your new hand. Balance clean vs dirty burracos based on game state.
strategy.advanced: Calculate optimal discard pile takes based on visible cards. Force opponents into difficult positions by holding key cards. Use the discard pile to manipulate what opponents can take. Advanced card counting to predict opponent hands.
tips: Always try to create at least one clean burraco for maximum points
Save wild cards for critical meld completions
Watch partner's melds and discards for coordination
Taking pozzetto directly lets you use cards immediately
Taking pozzetto indirectly hides your hand from partner influence
Going out quickly can deny opponents their pozzetto bonus
Track which cards have been played to predict opponents' needs

variations.name: Semipulito burraco bonus
variations.description: Some Italian circles score an intermediate bonus for a semipulito burraco: an 8+ card meld that contains exactly seven consecutive natural cards plus one wild card, or at least seven equal cards with a wild card, commonly worth 150 points with a distinct crosswise marker.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine-level differences for semipulito scoring are documented textually here and should be modeled explicitly when implementing.

variations.name: Stalemate must-draw resolution
variations.description: Instead of ending the hand when all four players in turn simply take the single discard and throw another card, some groups require that the next player in turn must break the stalemate by drawing from the stock pile so play continues.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation changes only how stalemates are resolved; engine overrides are left empty until a specific flow is modeled.

variations.name: Three-player Burraco
variations.description: A three-player version in which each player begins with 11 cards and there are two pozzetti: one of 18 cards and one of 11. The first player to meld out takes the 18-card pozzetto and continues alone while the remaining two form a partnership and compete using the smaller pozzetto.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Three-player structure is fully described in text; specific engine overrides (player count, partnerships, pozzetto sizes) are to be wired in when this variant is implemented.

variations.name: Two-player Burraco
variations.description: A head-to-head variant where each player is dealt 11 cards and there are two 11-card pozzetti. Play and scoring follow the standard Italian Burraco rules, but there are no partnerships, so each player manages melds and pozzetto timing alone.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Two-player head-to-head structure follows the main rules; implementation can add concrete overrides for player count and pozzetto handling later.

variations.name: Three-player scoring notes
variations.description: In some descriptions of three-player Burraco, the two players who become partners after the first pozzetto is taken divide their partnership total between them for cumulative scoring, rather than tracking a separate team score.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This entry records how some groups apportion scores in three-player games; engine scoring overrides are deferred to a dedicated implementation.

variations.name: Two-player positional play
variations.description: Two-player Burraco plays identically to the partnership game except that there is no benefit in exposing melds early unless it enables taking a pozzetto or prevents the opponent from closing before your next turn.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This describes common strategic guidance for two-player Burraco; there are no structural rule changes requiring immediate engine overrides.

scoring.description: Teams score the point values of all cards they have melded on the table, receive bonuses for burracos (clean or dirty) and for going out, and subtract the values of any cards left in hand. A clean burraco (seven or more natural cards) is worth 200 points, a dirty burraco (seven or more cards including at least one wild card) is worth 100 points, going out (closing) is worth 100 points, and a team that has not taken its pozzetto at the end of the hand loses 100 points.
scoring.winCondition: The game is played over multiple hands; after each hand both teams add their hand score (melded cards plus bonuses minus cards in hand and pozzetto penalties) to a cumulative total. When at least one team has more than 2000 points, the team with the higher total wins the game.
